summary: IGP Flexible Algorithm lets a network compute paths tuned to different goals. Originally it did not apply to ordinary IP forwarding. This document extends it so it can be used with regular IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding.

eli5.summary: A route app can offer the fastest or the cheapest road. This lets plain internet traffic use these custom route choices, not just special traffic.

questions: flex-algo for ipv4 and ipv6 without segment routing
what is the is-is ip algorithm sub-tlv
subtitle: Lets IGP Flexible Algorithm steer ordinary IPv4 and IPv6 traffic, not only Segment Routing traffic.

tldr.problem: IGP Flexible Algorithm computes constraint-based paths, but the base specification (RFC 9350) only covers Segment Routing data planes, so it cannot be deployed without SR or SRv6.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC adds IP as another Flex-Algorithm data plane. Routers advertise IP participation separately, and new IS-IS and OSPF advertisements tie an IPv4 or IPv6 prefix to a Flex-Algorithm value from 128 to 255 and a metric.
tldr.outcome: Traffic to an ordinary IP prefix can follow a path computed for a specific goal, such as lowest latency or highest bandwidth, without SR or SRv6.

today: RFC 9502 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the base specification in RFC 9350.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation
sections.content:
An IGP Flexible Algorithm lets an interior gateway protocol compute constraint-based paths. As specified in RFC 9350, it computes such paths to Flexible-Algorithm-specific Prefix Segment Identifiers (SIDs) and Flexible-Algorithm-specific SRv6 Locators. That means it cannot be deployed without SR or SRv6.

This document removes that dependency by letting Flexible Algorithm compute paths to IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes.

The RFC's use case is a 5G mobile network. Each end-user session from a gNodeB can go to a specific User Plane Function (UPF), and each UPF has a unique IP address. Associating that address with an algorithm lets a session take a path tuned for minimal latency or highest bandwidth, which helps meet a Service Level Agreement.
sections.eli5: Special delivery lanes used to need special trucks. This change lets any normal truck use them, as long as the street address is marked for that lane.

sections.title: Definitions and Participation
sections.content:
To keep forwarding loop-free, all routers in a Flex-Algorithm MUST agree on the Flexible Algorithm Definition (FAD). Selected nodes advertise FADs as described in RFC 9350. The FAD is data plane independent and is shared by all data planes.

Participation is different. A node that participates in a Flex-Algorithm can compute paths for it and is part of its topology. Participation is advertised for each data plane independently, and IP is treated as its own data plane. A router may take part in a Flex-Algorithm for IP but not for SR. Advertising IP participation does not affect participation in default algorithm 0, in which every router in an IGP domain takes part.
sections.eli5: Everyone agrees on the rules of the game first. Then each player says separately which games they join, so joining one game does not sign you up for another.

sections.title: Advertising Participation
sections.content:
Participation is advertised with a new element in each protocol.

  • IS-IS IP Algorithm Sub-TLV: type 29, inside the Router Capability TLV. It lists algorithm values, each one octet, from 128 to 255. It MUST NOT be advertised across level boundaries, so the S bit in the Router Capability TLV MUST NOT be set. It MUST NOT be advertised more than once at a level.
  • OSPF IP Algorithm TLV: type 21, a top-level TLV of the Router Information Opaque LSA. It MUST be advertised only once in the LSA. Area- or AS-scoped flooding is REQUIRED, and AS scope SHOULD NOT be used unless local policy calls for domain-wide flooding.

A receiver MUST ignore values outside 128 to 255 and SHOULD log this as an error. In both protocols the participation applies to all topologies in which the advertising node takes part. If several copies arrive, the receiver uses the first one (in IS-IS the first in the lowest-numbered LSP) and ignores later ones.
sections.eli5: Each router holds up a card listing which special lanes it will work in. The card can only list lane numbers from 128 to 255, and a router should hold up just one card.

sections.title: Advertising Prefix Reachability
sections.content:
Existing prefix advertisements cannot carry an algorithm, because they advertise reachability in default algorithm 0. So new advertisements are defined. Each carries an Algorithm and a Metric. The FAD's M-flag does not apply to them.

  • IS-IS: IPv4 Algorithm Prefix Reachability TLV (type 126) and IPv6 Algorithm Prefix Reachability TLV (type 127). Each prefix entry has a metric, flags, algorithm, prefix length and prefix. The D-flag is set when a prefix is leaked from level 2 to level 1, and such prefixes MUST NOT be leaked back to level 2, to prevent looping.
  • OSPFv2: IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability Sub-TLV (type 6, length 8) in the Extended Prefix TLV, and a separate IP Forwarding Address Sub-TLV (type 7, length 4), which applies only to AS External and NSSA External routes.
  • OSPFv3: IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability Sub-TLV (type 35, length 8). The NU-bit in the parent TLV's PrefixOptions MUST be set, or the receiver ignores the sub-TLV.

In OSPF a metric of 0XFFFFFFFF MUST be considered unreachable. Between areas, an ABR uses the new OSPF IP Flexible Algorithm ASBR Metric Sub-TLV (type 2 for OSPFv2, 36 for OSPFv3), because the SR-based FAAM Sub-TLV MUST NOT be used for IP Flex-Algorithm calculation.

Conflicts resolve conservatively. If different originators advertise the same prefix with different algorithms, all are ignored and no forwarding entries are installed. A plain algorithm 0 advertisement of the same prefix wins over the algorithm advertisement in OSPF and in IS-IS. If a prefix shows up in both an SRv6 Locator and an IP algorithm advertisement, both are ignored.
sections.eli5: Each address gets a sticker naming its lane and a cost number. If two routers put different lane stickers on the same address, everyone ignores both. A normal sticker always beats a special one.

sections.title: Path Calculation and Forwarding
sections.content:
IP Flexible Algorithm is treated as one more data plane of Flexible Algorithm. Path calculation follows RFC 9350, uses only the IP data plane participation, and is independent of the calculation for SR or SRv6. When computing paths for a Flex-Algorithm, every node that does not advertise IP participation MUST be pruned from the topology.

The prefix advertisement carries a topology identifier (MTID) and an Algorithm value, so the path to the prefix MUST be computed with that Flex-Algorithm in that topology. Forwarding entries MUST be installed in routers that participate in the matching topology and algorithm, and MUST NOT be installed for Flex-Algorithms in which the node does not participate.
sections.eli5: When planning a route, a router ignores every road that has not signed up for the special lane. It only puts the route in its map if it is part of that lane.

sections.title: Coexistence and Protection
sections.content:
Several data planes can use the same Flex-Algorithm value and share its FAD. SR-MPLS traffic follows Flex-Algorithm-specific SR SIDs, while IP traffic follows the Flex-Algorithm-specific prefix advertisements. For one prefix in one Flex-Algorithm, paths are calculated and installed for a single data plane only. Because participation and calculation are data plane specific, forwarding stays consistent among all nodes that apply the algorithm to that data plane.

For protection, the RFC notes that IGP restoration is often fast enough, possibly helped by Equal Cost Multipath (ECMP). Where more is wanted, operators can use Loop-Free Alternates (RFC 5286) or Remote Loop-Free Alternates (RFC 7490). Their computations MUST stay inside the Flex-Algorithm topology.
sections.eli5: Different kinds of traffic can share the same special lane rules. If a road breaks, backup roads are allowed, but only ones that are also part of the same lane.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
This document inherits the security considerations of RFC 9350 and adds one new way to disrupt Flexible Algorithm networks. An attacker can suppress reachability of a prefix that a legitimate node advertises for IP Flex-Algorithm X by advertising the same prefix in Flex-Algorithm Y from a malicious node, since conflicting algorithms cause the advertisements to be ignored.

The existing authentication extensions for IS-IS, OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 address this. If an authenticated node is taken over, authentication cannot stop the attack, which is no different from that node advertising any other incorrect information.
sections.eli5: A trickster could write a different lane on someone else's address and make everyone ignore it. Passwords between routers stop outsiders, but not a router that was taken over.
